test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (JSO) 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is an absolute measure of skewness?
solution:
The correct answer is **Mean - Median.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mean - Median:**

 
 
• This is an absolute measure of skewness. It directly measures the difference between the mean and median of a data set.
 
• In a financial enterprise, understanding skewness is essential for risk management and investment decisions. For instance, a positive skewness might indicate potential for higher returns, but also higher risk.
 
• The absolute measure helps in identifying whether the data is skewed to the left or right without considering the size of the data set.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **(Mean - Median) / standard deviation:**

 
 
• This is a relative measure of skewness, known as the Pearson’s first coefficient of skewness. It standardizes the skewness by the standard deviation, making it a unitless measure.
 
• While useful, it is not an absolute measure and can be affected by the scale of the data set.
 
 
 
• **(Q3 + Q1 - 2Q2) / standard deviation:**
 
 
• This is another form of relative measure of skewness, known as the Bowley’s coefficient of skewness. It uses quartiles to determine the skewness.
 
• It is also not an absolute measure and is influenced by the dispersion of the data.
 
 
 
• **(Mean - Mode) / standard deviation:**
 
 
• This is the Pearson’s second coefficient of skewness, another relative measure that uses the mode instead of the median.
 
• Like the other relative measures, it is standardized by the standard deviation and does not provide an absolute measure of skewness.
